summary: Mandatory exploration can become ceremony, and stakeholders can answer confidently without resolving the underlying uncertainty.

points.text: For reversible, low-risk tasks, the cost of an interview and specification may exceed the cost of producing a small prototype and learning from concrete feedback.
Users may not know hidden constraints or edge cases; recording their first answer can freeze a mistaken assumption rather than discover the real need.
An agent can generate plausible but leading questions that bias stakeholders toward its preferred implementation and create false confidence in alignment.
Long exploration queues increase time to first evidence and encourage specification drift if the repository changes before execution starts.
